title: $t$-tone colorings of outerplanar and Halin graphs
summary: A $t$-tone $k$-coloring of a graph $G$ assigns a set of $t$ distinct colors from $\{1, \dots, k\}$ to each vertex so that vertices at distance $d$ share fewer than $d$ common colors. The $t$-tone chromatic number of $G$ is the minimum $k$ such that $G$ has a $t$-tone $k$-coloring. This paper investigates the $t$-tone coloring of two specific subclasses of planar graphs: subcubic outerplanar graphs and Halin graphs. We provide a complete characterization of the $2$-tone chromatic number for subcubic outerplanar graphs and establish a sharp upper bound for their $3$-tone chromatic number. We…
